## 1. `wasserstein_1d`

Two normal samples.

```{r}
set.seed(2026)

n_pts <- 100

sample1 <- rnorm(n_pts, 0, 1)
sample2 <- rnorm(n_pts, 2, 1)
```

```{r}
# Combine into a single long-format data frame
df <- data.frame(
  value = c(sample1, sample2),
  group = rep(c("Sample 1", "Sample 2"), each = n_pts)
)

# Plot overlapping density curves
ggplot(df, aes(x = value, fill = group)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Density Plot of Sample 1 and Sample 2",
    x = "Value",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "Distribution"
  )
```

Wasserstein distance between the two samples.

```{r}
wasserstein1d(sample1, sample2)
```

Visualize the transport map by point-to-point segments

```{r}
# Sorted samples for perfect 1D coupling
gamma <- sort(sample1)
mu <- sort(sample2)

df_transport <- data.frame(
  source = gamma,
  target = mu
)

ggplot(df_transport) +
  # Draw the transport paths
  geom_segment(aes(x = source, xend = target, y = 1, yend = 0), 
               alpha = 0.3, color = "blue") +
  # Draw the actual data points
  geom_point(aes(x = source, y = 1), color = "black", size = 1.5) +
  geom_point(aes(x = target, y = 0), color = "red", size = 1.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, 1), labels = c("Target (mu)", "Base (gamma)")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Optimal Transport Map", x = "Value", y = "") +
  theme(panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank())
```

Visualize the logarithmic map by tangent vector lollipop chart.

```{r}
# The tangent vector
tangent_v <- mu - gamma

df_log <- data.frame(
  gamma = gamma,
  displacement = tangent_v
)

ggplot(df_log, aes(x = gamma, y = displacement)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = gamma, yend = 0), color = "gray50") +
  geom_point(color = "darkgreen", size = 2) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Logarithmic Map: Displacement Vectors", 
    x = "Base Measure Coordinates", 
    y = "Tangent Vector (Displacement)"
  )
```

Visualize the exponential map by geodesic interpolation.
In the Shiny app, the user will morph gamma to mu by using the time bar.

```{r}
# Define time steps
t_steps <- seq(0, 1, by = 0.25)

# Apply the exponential map at each time step
df_exp <- lapply(t_steps, function(t) {
  data.frame(
    # exp_gamma(t * v) = gamma + t * v
    value = gamma + t * tangent_v, 
    t_label = as.factor(t)
  )
}) |> bind_rows()

ggplot(df_exp, aes(x = value, fill = t_label, group = t_label)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5, color = "white", size = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "plasma", name = "Time (t)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Exponential Map: Geodesic Path from Sample 1 to Sample 2", 
    x = "Value", 
    y = "Density"
  )
```





## 2. `frechet_mean`

```{r}
set.seed(2026)

n_pts <- 100
samples <- lapply(1:10, function(i) {
  shift <- runif(n = 1, min = -1, max = 1)
  c(rnorm(n_pts * 0.1, mean = 0 + shift, sd = 1), 
    rnorm(n_pts * 0.6, mean = 5 + shift, sd = 1),
    rnorm(n_pts * 0.3, mean = 10 + shift, sd = 1))
})

# Combine for plotting
df_samples <- bind_rows(lapply(1:10, function(i) {
  data.frame(value = samples[[i]], type = "Original Samples", group = paste("Sample", i))
}))
```

```{r}
# 1. Exact 1D Fréchet Mean
mean_exact <- frechet_mean_1d_exact(samples, n_grid = n_pts)

# 2. Steepest Descent Fréchet Mean
# Initialize with the first sample
mean_iterative <- frechet_mean_1d_steepest_descent(
  gamma_init = samples[[1]], 
  target_samples = samples, 
  max_iter = 50, 
  tol = 1e-4
)

# Format outputs for ggplot
df_exact <- data.frame(
  value = mean_exact, 
  type = "Exact Fréchet Mean", 
  group = "Exact"
)

df_iterative <- data.frame(
  value = mean_iterative, 
  type = "Steepest Descent", 
  group = "Iterative"
)

df_plot <- bind_rows(df_samples, df_exact, df_iterative)
```

In Shiny app, every iteration, i.e., the progress of steepest descent process will be shown.

```{r}
ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = value, group = group, color = type, size = type, linetype = type)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Original Samples" = "gray90", 
    "Exact Fréchet Mean" = "dodgerblue", 
    "Steepest Descent" = "darkorange"
  )) +
  scale_size_manual(values = c(
    "Original Samples" = 0.8, 
    "Exact Fréchet Mean" = 2, 
    "Steepest Descent" = 1.2
  )) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(
    "Original Samples" = "dashed", 
    "Exact Fréchet Mean" = "solid", 
    "Steepest Descent" = "twodash"
  )) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Fréchet Barycenter of Bimodal Distributions",
    subtitle = "Comparing Exact Quantile Averaging vs. Steepest Descent",
    x = "Value",
    y = "Density",
    color = "Distribution Type",
    size = "Distribution Type",
    linetype = "Distribution Type"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```





## 3. Wasserstein Distance and Barycenter for 2d Distributions

2d point clouds.

```{r}
set.seed(2026)

n_pts <- 100

x <- rnorm(n = 3, mean = 0, sd = 2)
y <- rnorm(n = 3, mean = 0, sd = 2)

# Create 3 point clouds shifted in a triangle formation
cloud1 <- cbind(rnorm(n_pts, x[1], 0.5), rnorm(n_pts, y[1], 0.5))
cloud2 <- cbind(rnorm(n_pts, x[2], 0.5), rnorm(n_pts, y[2], 0.5))
cloud3 <- cbind(rnorm(n_pts, x[3], 0.5), rnorm(n_pts, y[3], 0.5))

targets <- list(cloud1, cloud2, cloud3)
```

```{r}
# Initialize the descent at the first point cloud
barycenter <- frechet_mean_2d_steepest(
  gamma_init = cloud1, 
  target_samples = targets, 
  max_iter = 100, 
  tol = 1e-5
)
```

```{r}
# Combine original target clouds for plotting
df_clouds <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(x = cloud1[,1], y = cloud1[,2], group = "Cloud 1"),
  data.frame(x = cloud2[,1], y = cloud2[,2], group = "Cloud 2"),
  data.frame(x = cloud3[,1], y = cloud3[,2], group = "Cloud 3")
)

# Format barycenter data
df_bary <- data.frame(x = barycenter[,1], y = barycenter[,2], group = "Fréchet Mean")

# Map the barycenter to Cloud 1 to extract the transport segments
mapped_cloud1 <- transport_map_2d(barycenter, cloud1)

df_segments <- data.frame(
  x_start = barycenter[,1],
  y_start = barycenter[,2],
  x_end   = mapped_cloud1[,1],
  y_end   = mapped_cloud1[,2]
)
```

```{r}
ggplot() +
  # 1. Draw optimal transport segments from the barycenter to Cloud 1
  geom_segment(data = df_segments, 
               aes(x = x_start, y = y_start, xend = x_end, yend = y_end), 
               color = "gray70", alpha = 0.6) +
               
  # 2. Plot the original target point clouds
  geom_point(data = df_clouds, aes(x = x, y = y, color = group), 
             alpha = 0.5, size = 2) +
             
  # 3. Plot the computed Fréchet mean
  geom_point(data = df_bary, aes(x = x, y = y, color = group), 
             size = 3, shape = 17) +
             
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Cloud 1" = "dodgerblue",
    "Cloud 2" = "firebrick",
    "Cloud 3" = "forestgreen",
    "Fréchet Mean" = "black"
  )) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "2D Fréchet Mean of Point Clouds",
    subtitle = "Triangles represent the mean. Gray lines trace the optimal transport map to Cloud 1.",
    x = "Coordinate 1",
    y = "Coordinate 2",
    color = "Distribution"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```
